sanskrit: kṣatriyeṣv āśrito dharmaḥ prajānāṃ paripālanam kṣatrād vṛttir brāhmaṇānāṃ taiḥ kathaṃ brāhmaṇo varaḥ
english: In the Kṣatriyas resides dharma — the protection of the people; and from the Kṣatriya comes the livelihood of the Brāhmaṇas. By what reckoning, then, is the Brāhmaṇa the greater?

sanskrit: sarvabhūtapradhānāṃs tān bhaikṣavṛttīn ahaṃ sadā ātmasaṃbhāvitān viprān sthāpayāmy ātmano vaśe
english: Those Brāhmaṇas who deem themselves the foremost of all beings, yet live by begging and are puffed up with their own conceit — them I ever hold in subjection to my will.

sanskrit: kathitaṃ hy anayā satyaṃ gāyatryā kanyayā divi vijeṣyāmy avaśān sarvān brāhmaṇāṃś carmavāsasaḥ
english: For the truth has been spoken in heaven by this maiden, the Gāyatrī: I shall conquer all the unruly Brāhmaṇas, those clad in hides.

sanskrit: na ca māṃ cyāvayed rāṣṭrāt triṣu lokeṣu kaś cana devo vā mānuṣo vāpi tasmāj jyeṣṭho dvijād aham
english: In the three worlds no one could cast me out from my realm — neither god nor man. Therefore am I superior to the twice-born.

sanskrit: adya brahmottaraṃ lokaṃ kariṣye kṣatriyottaram na hi me saṃyuge kaś cit soḍhum utsahate balam
english: This day I shall make the world, which holds the Brāhmaṇa supreme, a world in which the Kṣatriya is supreme; for no one in battle has the power to withstand my might.

sanskrit: arjunasya vacaḥ śrutvā vitrastābhūn niśācarī athainam antarikṣasthas tato vāyur abhāṣata
english: Hearing Arjuna's words, the night-ranging spirit was struck with terror. Then Vāyu, abiding in the sky, addressed him.

sanskrit: tyajainaṃ kaluṣaṃ bhāvaṃ brāhmaṇebhyo namaskuru eteṣāṃ kurvataḥ pāpaṃ rāṣṭrakṣobho hi te bhavet
english: Cast off this defiled disposition and bow before the Brāhmaṇas; for if you do them wrong, ruin will come upon your kingdom.

sanskrit: atha vā tvāṃ mahīpāla śamayiṣyanti vai dvijāḥ nirasiṣyanti vā rāṣṭrād dhatotsāhaṃ mahābalāḥ
english: Else, O lord of the earth, the twice-born, mighty in power, will subdue you, or will drive you from your realm, your spirit broken.

sanskrit: taṃ rājā kas tvam ity āha tatas taṃ prāha mārutaḥ vāyur vai devadūto 'smi hitaṃ tvāṃ prabravīmy aham
english: The king said to him, 'Who are you?' Then the Wind-god replied to him: 'I am Vāyu, the messenger of the gods; I speak to you for your good.'

sanskrit: arjuna uvāca aho tvayādya vipreṣu bhaktirāgaḥ pradarśitaḥ yādṛśaṃ pṛthivī bhūtaṃ tādṛśaṃ brūhi vai dvijam
english: Arjuna said: Ah, what devoted attachment to the Brāhmaṇas you have shown this day! Tell me, then — to what created thing is the Brāhmaṇa like? Is he as the earth?

sanskrit: vāyor vā sadṛśaṃ kiṃ cid brūhi tvaṃ brāhmaṇottamam apāṃ vai sadṛśaṃ brūhi sūryasya nabhaso 'pi vā
english: Or tell me, is the best of Brāhmaṇas in any way like the wind? Tell me — is he like the waters, or like the sun, or like the sky?

sanskrit: vāyur uvāca śṛṇu mūḍha guṇān kāṃś cid brāhmaṇānāṃ mahātmanām ye tvayā kīrtitā rājaṃs tebhyo 'tha brāhmaṇo varaḥ
english: Vāyu said: Hear, O fool, some of the virtues of the high-souled Brāhmaṇas. By those very things you have named, O king, the Brāhmaṇa is shown to be the greater.

sanskrit: tyaktvā mahītvaṃ bhūmis tu spardhayāṅganṛpasya ha nāśaṃ jagāma tāṃ vipro vyaṣṭambhayata kaśyapaḥ
english: When the Earth, through rivalry with king Aṅga, forsook her own earthhood and went to ruin, the Brāhmaṇa Kaśyapa upheld her once again.

sanskrit: akṣayā brāhmaṇā rājan divi ceha ca nityadā apibat tejasā hy āpaḥ svayam evāṅgirāḥ purā
english: Imperishable are the Brāhmaṇas, O king, in heaven and on earth forever. Of old, Aṅgiras himself drank up the waters by his own fiery power.

sanskrit: sa tāḥ piban kṣīram iva nātṛpyata mahātapāḥ apūrayan mahaughena mahīṃ sarvāṃ ca pārthiva
english: Drinking them as though they were milk, the great ascetic was not sated; and then with a mighty flood he filled the whole earth again, O son of Pṛthā.

sanskrit: tasminn ahaṃ ca kruddhe vai jagat tyaktvā tato gataḥ vyatiṣṭham agnihotre ca ciram aṅgiraso bhayāt
english: When he was wroth, I too forsook the world and departed, and for a long while took refuge in the agnihotra fire, in fear of Aṅgiras.

sanskrit: abhiśaptaś ca bhagavān gautamena puraṃdaraḥ ahalyāṃ kāmayāno vai dharmārthaṃ ca na hiṃsitaḥ
english: Even the lord Purandara was cursed by Gautama when he lusted after Ahalyā; yet for the sake of dharma he was not slain.

sanskrit: tathā samudro nṛpate pūrṇo mṛṣṭena vāriṇā brāhmaṇair abhiśaptaḥ saṃl lavaṇodaḥ kṛto vibho
english: So too the ocean, O king, once full of sweet water, was cursed by the Brāhmaṇas and made into a sea of salt, O mighty one.

sanskrit: suvarṇavarṇo nirdhūmaḥ saṃhatordhvaśikhaḥ kaviḥ kruddhenāṅgirasā śapto guṇair etair vivarjitaḥ
english: Fire — gold-hued, smokeless, its flame leaping upward in a single mass, the wise one — was cursed by the wrathful Aṅgiras and stripped of these very qualities.

sanskrit: marutaś cūrṇitān paśya ye 'hasanta mahodadhim suvarṇadhāriṇā nityam avaśaptā dvijātinā
english: Behold the Maruts ground to dust, who once laughed at the great ocean — cursed forever by the gold-bearing twice-born one.

sanskrit: samo na tvaṃ dvijātibhyaḥ śreṣṭhaṃ viddhi narādhipa garbhasthān brāhmaṇān samyaṅ namasyati kila prabhuḥ
english: You are not the equal of the twice-born; know them to be supreme, O ruler of men. The Lord himself, they say, duly does reverence to Brāhmaṇas while they are yet in the womb.

sanskrit: daṇḍakānāṃ mahad rājyaṃ brāhmaṇena vināśitam tālajaṅghaṃ mahat kṣatram aurveṇaikena nāśitam
english: The great kingdom of the Daṇḍakas was destroyed by a Brāhmaṇa; the great Kṣatriya host of the Tālajaṅghas was destroyed by Aurva alone.

sanskrit: tvayā ca vipulaṃ rājyaṃ balaṃ dharmaḥ śrutaṃ tathā dattātreyaprasādena prāptaṃ paramadurlabham
english: And by you a vast kingdom, strength, dharma, and learning — gifts most hard to win — were obtained through the grace of Dattātreya.

sanskrit: agniṃ tvaṃ yajase nityaṃ kasmād arjuna brāhmaṇam sa hi sarvasya lokasya havyavāṭ kiṃ na vetsi tam
english: You ever worship Fire, O Arjuna — and what is Fire but a Brāhmaṇa? For he is the bearer of oblations for all the world. Do you not know him?

sanskrit: atha vā brāhmaṇaśreṣṭham anu bhūtānupālakam kartāraṃ jīvalokasya kasmāj jānan vimuhyase
english: Or, knowing him to be the foremost of Brāhmaṇas, the protector of beings, the maker of the world of the living — why are you, knowing this, so bewildered?

sanskrit: tathā prajāpatir brahmā avyaktaḥ prabhavāpyayaḥ yenedaṃ nikhilaṃ viśvaṃ janitaṃ sthāvaraṃ caram
english: So too is Brahmā, the Lord of creatures, the Unmanifest, the source and the dissolution of all, by whom this entire universe, moving and unmoving, was brought forth.

sanskrit: aṇḍajātaṃ tu brahmāṇaṃ ke cid icchanty apaṇḍitāḥ aṇḍād bhinnād babhuḥ śailā diśo 'mbhaḥ pṛthivī divam
english: Some, the unlearned, hold that Brahmā was born from an egg, and that from the egg, when it split, came the mountains, the quarters, the waters, the earth, and the sky.

sanskrit: draṣṭavyaṃ naitad evaṃ hi kathaṃ jyāyastamo hi saḥ smṛtam ākāśam aṇḍaṃ tu tasmāj jātaḥ pitāmahaḥ
english: But it is not to be regarded thus — for how could he, the very greatest, be so born? Space itself is remembered as the egg, and from it the Grandsire came forth.

sanskrit: tiṣṭhet katham iti brūhi na kiṃ cid dhi tadā bhavet ahaṃkāra iti proktaḥ sarvatejogataḥ prabhuḥ
english: Tell me — on what could it have rested? At that time nothing whatever existed. He is named Ego (ahaṃkāra), the Lord in whom all radiance dwells.

sanskrit: nāsty aṇḍam asti tu brahmā sa rājaṃl lokabhāvanaḥ ity uktaḥ sa tadā tūṣṇīm abhūd vāyus tam abravīt
english: There is no egg; there is only Brahmā, O king, the maker of the worlds. Thus addressed, the king then fell silent, and Vāyu spoke to him again.

sanskrit: vāyur uvāca imāṃ bhūmiṃ brāhmaṇebhyo ditsur vai dakṣiṇāṃ purā aṅgo nāma nṛpo rājaṃs tataś cintāṃ mahī yayau
english: Vāyu said: Long ago a king named Aṅga wished to give this earth as a sacrificial gift to the Brāhmaṇas; and at that, O king, the Earth fell into anxious thought.

sanskrit: dhāraṇīṃ sarvabhūtānām ayaṃ prāpya varo nṛpaḥ katham icchati māṃ dātuṃ dvijebhyo brahmaṇaḥ sutām
english: 'Having obtained me, the bearer of all beings — how does this best of kings desire to give me, the daughter of Brahmā, away to the twice-born?'

sanskrit: sāhaṃ tyaktvā gamiṣyāmi bhūmitvaṃ brahmaṇaḥ padam ayaṃ sarāṣṭro nṛpatir mā bhūd iti tato 'gamat
english: 'Forsaking my earthhood, I shall go to the abode of Brahmā — let not this king keep his realm.' And so she departed.

sanskrit: tatas tāṃ kaśyapo dṛṣṭvā vrajantīṃ pṛthivīṃ tadā praviveśa mahīṃ sadyo muktvātmānaṃ samāhitaḥ
english: Then Kaśyapa, seeing the Earth thus departing, at once entered into her, releasing his own self, his mind composed.

sanskrit: ruddhā sā sarvato jajñe tṛṇauṣadhisamanvitā dharmottarā naṣṭabhayā bhūmir āsīt tato nṛpa
english: Held fast on every side, she came forth again endowed with grass and herbs; and the Earth, O king, became rich in dharma and free from fear.

sanskrit: evaṃ varṣasahasrāṇi divyāni vipulavrataḥ triṃśataṃ kaśyapo rājan bhūmir āsīd atandritaḥ
english: Thus for thirty thousand divine years, O king, Kaśyapa of vast vows was the Earth, untiring.

sanskrit: athāgamya mahārāja namaskṛtya ca kaśyapam pṛthivī kāśyapī jajñe sutā tasya mahātmanaḥ
english: Then, O great king, the Earth came and made obeisance to Kaśyapa, and so became Kāśyapī, the daughter of that high-souled one.

sanskrit: eṣa rājann īdṛśo vai brāhmaṇaḥ kaśyapo 'bhavat anyaṃ prabrūhi vāpi tvaṃ kaśyapāt kṣatriyaṃ varam
english: Such, O king, was that Brāhmaṇa Kaśyapa. Now name me, if you can, any Kṣatriya greater than Kaśyapa.

sanskrit: tūṣṇīṃ babhūva nṛpatiḥ pavanas tv abravīt punaḥ śṛṇu rājann utathyasya jātasyāṅgirase kule
english: The king fell silent, and the Wind-god spoke again: Hear now, O king, of Utathya, born in the line of Aṅgiras.

sanskrit: bhadrā somasya duhitā rūpeṇa paramā matā tasyās tulyaṃ patiṃ soma utathyaṃ samapaśyata
english: Bhadrā, the daughter of Soma, was deemed peerless in beauty; and Soma saw in Utathya a husband worthy of her.

sanskrit: sā ca tīvraṃ tapas tepe mahābhāgā yaśasvinī utathyaṃ tu mahābhāgaṃ tatkṛte 'varayat tadā
english: And that illustrious, glorious lady practised fierce austerities, and for that end she chose the great-souled Utathya.

sanskrit: tata āhūya sotathyaṃ dadāv atra yaśasvinīm bhāryārthe sa ca jagrāha vidhivad bhūridakṣiṇa
english: Then Soma summoned Utathya and gave the glorious maiden to him to wife; and he, the giver of bounteous gifts, received her duly.

sanskrit: tāṃ tv akāmayata śrīmān varuṇaḥ pūrvam eva ha sa cāgamya vanaprasthaṃ yamunāyāṃ jahāra tām
english: But the glorious Varuṇa had desired her even before; and coming to the forest-dwelling, he carried her off at the Yamunā.

sanskrit: jaleśvaras tu hṛtvā tām anayat svapuraṃ prati paramādbhutasaṃkāśaṃ ṣaṭsahasraśatahradam
english: The lord of waters, having seized her, bore her away toward his own city — a city of utmost wonder, with six hundred thousand lakes.

sanskrit: na hi ramyataraṃ kiṃ cit tasmād anyat purottamam prāsādair apsarobhiś ca divyaiḥ kāmaiś ca śobhitam tatra devas tayā sārdhaṃ reme rājañ jaleśvaraḥ
english: There was no lovelier place than that finest of cities, adorned with palaces, with apsarases, and with divine delights; and there the god, the lord of waters, took his pleasure with her, O king.

sanskrit: athākhyātam utathyāya tataḥ patnyavamardanam
english: Then the violation of his wife was made known to Utathya.

sanskrit: tac chrutvā nāradāt sarvam utathyo nāradaṃ tadā provāca gaccha brūhi tvaṃ varuṇaṃ paruṣaṃ vacaḥ madvākyān muñca me bhāryāṃ kasmād vā hṛtavān asi
english: Hearing all this from Nārada, Utathya said to Nārada: 'Go and speak harsh words to Varuṇa — by my command, release my wife! Why have you carried her off?'

sanskrit: lokapālo 'si lokānāṃ na lokasya vilopakaḥ somena dattā bhāryā me tvayā cāpahṛtādya vai
english: 'You are a guardian of the worlds, not a despoiler of the world. My wife was given me by Soma, and this day you have stolen her away.'

sanskrit: ity ukto vacanāt tasya nāradena jaleśvaraḥ muñca bhāryām utathyasyety atha taṃ varuṇo 'bravīt mamaiṣā supriyā bhāryā nainām utsraṣṭum utsahe
english: Thus addressed by Nārada in Utathya's words — 'Release Utathya's wife!' — Varuṇa replied: 'She is my own dear wife; I cannot bring myself to give her up.'

sanskrit: ity ukto varuṇenātha nāradaḥ prāpya taṃ munim utathyam abravīd vākyaṃ nātihṛṣṭamanā iva
english: So answered by Varuṇa, Nārada came back to the sage Utathya and spoke to him, his heart none too glad.

sanskrit: gale gṛhītvā kṣipto 'smi varuṇena mahāmune na prayacchati te bhāryāṃ yat te kāryaṃ kuruṣva tat
english: 'Seizing me by the throat, Varuṇa has flung me out, O great sage. He will not give you your wife — do what you must.'

sanskrit: nāradasya vacaḥ śrutvā kruddhaḥ prājvalad aṅgirāḥ apibat tejasā vāri viṣṭabhya sumahātapāḥ
english: Hearing Nārada's words, the descendant of Aṅgiras blazed up in wrath; and that mighty ascetic, holding them fast, drank up the waters by his fiery power.

sanskrit: pīyamāne ca sarvasmiṃs toye vai salileśvaraḥ suhṛdbhiḥ kṣipyamāṇo 'pi naivāmuñcata tāṃ tadā
english: And as all the waters were being drunk up, the lord of the waters, though pressed by his friends, would still not release her then.

sanskrit: tataḥ kruddho 'bravīd bhūmim utathyo brāhmaṇottamaḥ darśayasva sthalaṃ bhadre ṣaṭsahasraśatahradam
english: Then Utathya, best of Brāhmaṇas, wrathfully commanded the Earth: 'Show me dry ground, O gentle one, where now there are six hundred thousand lakes!'

sanskrit: tatas tad iriṇaṃ jātaṃ samudraś cāpasarpitaḥ tasmād deśān nadīṃ caiva provācāsau dvijottamaḥ
english: Then that place became a barren waste, and the sea drew back; and from that region the best of the twice-born addressed the river as well.

sanskrit: adṛśyā gaccha bhīru tvaṃ sarasvati maruṃ prati apuṇya eṣa bhavatu deśas tyaktas tvayā śubhe
english: 'Vanish from sight, O timid Sarasvatī, and flow toward the desert; let this region, forsaken by you, O fair one, become unholy.'

sanskrit: tasmin saṃcūrṇite deśe bhadrām ādāya vāripaḥ adadāc charaṇaṃ gatvā bhāryām āṅgirasāya vai
english: When that region was thus laid waste, the lord of waters, taking up Bhadrā, came seeking refuge and gave the wife back to the son of Aṅgiras.

sanskrit: pratigṛhya tu tāṃ bhāryām utathyaḥ sumanābhavat mumoca ca jagad duḥkhād varuṇaṃ caiva haihaya
english: Receiving his wife again, Utathya was glad at heart, and he freed the world — and Varuṇa with it — from its distress, O Haihaya.

sanskrit: tataḥ sa labdhvā tāṃ bhāryāṃ varuṇaṃ prāha dharmavit utathyaḥ sumahātejā yat tac chṛṇu narādhipa
english: Then, having recovered his wife, Utathya — knower of dharma, of mighty splendor — spoke to Varuṇa; hear what he said, O ruler of men.

sanskrit: mayaiṣā tapasā prāptā krośatas te jalādhipa ity uktvā tām upādāya svam eva bhavanaṃ yayau
english: 'By my austerity I have won her back, O lord of waters, while you cried out in vain.' So saying, he took her up and went to his own dwelling.

sanskrit: eṣa rājann īdṛśo vai utathyo brāhmaṇarṣabhaḥ bravīmy ahaṃ brūhi vā tvam utathyāt kṣatriyaṃ varam
english: Such, O king, was that Utathya, that bull among Brāhmaṇas. So I declare — now name me, if you can, any Kṣatriya greater than Utathya.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca ity uktaḥ sa tadā tūṣṇīm abhūd vāyus tato 'bravīt śṛṇu rājann agastyasya māhātmyaṃ brāhmaṇasya ha
english: Bhīṣma said: Thus addressed, the king fell silent, and Vāyu then spoke: Hear, O king, the greatness of the Brāhmaṇa Agastya.

sanskrit: asurair nirjitā devā nirutsāhāś ca te kṛtāḥ yajñāś caiṣāṃ hṛtāḥ sarve pitṛbhyaś ca svadhā tathā
english: The gods, vanquished by the Asuras, were robbed of their spirit; all their sacrifices were carried off, and likewise the svadhā offering to the ancestors.

sanskrit: karmejyā mānavānāṃ ca dānavair haihayarṣabha bhraṣṭaiśvaryās tato devāś ceruḥ pṛthvīm iti śrutiḥ
english: And the rites and sacrifices of men were seized by the Dānavas, O bull of the Haihayas. Then the gods, fallen from their sovereignty, wandered the earth — so says the sacred tradition.

sanskrit: tataḥ kadā cit te rājan dīptam ādityavarcasam dadṛśus tejasā yuktam agastyaṃ vipulavratam
english: Then once, O king, they beheld Agastya of vast vows, blazing with the splendor of the sun, endowed with fiery glory.

sanskrit: abhivādya ca taṃ devā dṛṣṭvā ca yaśasā vṛtam idam ūcur mahātmānaṃ vākyaṃ kāle janādhipa
english: And the gods, having saluted him and seen him girt with glory, spoke this word to the high-souled one at the fitting time, O ruler of men.

sanskrit: dānavair yudhi bhagnāḥ sma tathaiśvaryāc ca bhraṃśitāḥ tad asmān no bhayāt tīvrāt trāhi tvaṃ munipuṃgava
english: 'We have been broken in battle by the Dānavas and cast down from our sovereignty. Deliver us, therefore, from this dire fear, O foremost of sages!'

sanskrit: ity uktaḥ sa tadā devair agastyaḥ kupito 'bhavat prajajvāla ca tejasvī kālāgnir iva saṃkṣaye
english: Thus addressed by the gods, Agastya then grew wroth, and the resplendent one blazed up like the fire of Time at the world's dissolution.

sanskrit: tena dīptāṃśujālena nirdagdhā dānavās tadā antarikṣān mahārāja nyapatanta sahasraśaḥ
english: By that web of blazing rays the Dānavas were then consumed, and from the sky, O great king, they fell in their thousands.

sanskrit: dahyamānās tu te daityās tasyāgastyasya tejasā ubhau lokau parityajya yayuḥ kāṣṭhāṃ sma dakṣiṇām
english: Burning in the fiery power of Agastya, those Daityas forsook both worlds and fled to the southern quarter.

sanskrit: balis tu yajate yajñam aśvamedhaṃ mahīṃ gataḥ ye 'nye svasthā mahīsthāś ca te na dagdhā mahāsurāḥ
english: But Bali, having gone into the earth, was performing the horse-sacrifice; and the other great Asuras who were at ease and dwelt within the earth were not consumed.

sanskrit: tato lokāḥ punaḥ prāptāḥ suraiḥ śāntaṃ ca tad rajaḥ athainam abruvan devā bhūmiṣṭhān asurāñ jahi
english: Then the worlds were regained by the gods, and that turmoil was stilled. Thereupon the gods said to him: 'Slay also the Asuras who dwell within the earth.'

sanskrit: ity ukta āha devān sa na śaknomi mahīgatān dagdhuṃ tapo hi kṣīyen me dhakṣyāmīti ca pārthiva
english: So addressed, he answered the gods: 'I cannot burn those who have gone into the earth, for were I to burn them, my austerity would be spent,' O son of Pṛthā.

sanskrit: evaṃ dagdhā bhagavatā dānavāḥ svena tejasā agastyena tadā rājaṃs tapasā bhāvitātmanā
english: Thus, O king, were the Dānavas burnt by the lord Agastya through his own fiery power, by him whose soul was perfected through austerity.

sanskrit: īdṛśaś cāpy agastyo hi kathitas te mayānagha bravīmy ahaṃ brūhi vā tvam agastyāt kṣatriyaṃ varam
english: Such, O sinless one, was Agastya, of whom I have told you. So I declare — now name me, if you can, any Kṣatriya greater than Agastya.

sanskrit: ity uktaḥ sa tadā tūṣṇīm abhūd vāyus tato 'bravīt śṛṇu rājan vasiṣṭhasya mukhyaṃ karma yaśasvinaḥ
english: Thus addressed, the king fell silent, and Vāyu then spoke: Hear, O king, of the chief deed of the glorious Vasiṣṭha.

sanskrit: ādityāḥ satram āsanta saro vai mānasaṃ prati vasiṣṭhaṃ manasā gatvā śrutvā tatrāsya gocaram
english: The Ādityas were holding a sacrificial session near the Mānasa lake, having approached Vasiṣṭha in their minds and learned that the place lay within his domain.

sanskrit: yajamānāṃs tu tān dṛṣṭvā vyagrān dīkṣānukarśitān hantum icchanti śailābhāḥ khalino nāma dānavāḥ
english: But seeing them sacrificing, intent and worn thin by their consecration, certain Dānavas called the Khalins, huge as mountains, desired to slay them.

sanskrit: adūrāt tu tatas teṣāṃ brahmadattavaraṃ saraḥ hatā hatā vai te tatra jīvanty āplutya dānavāḥ
english: Not far from there was a lake granted as a boon by Brahmā; and those Dānavas, slain again and again, would yet live, plunging into it and rising up.

sanskrit: te pragṛhya mahāghorān parvatān parighān drumān vikṣobhayantaḥ salilam utthitāḥ śatayojanam
english: Seizing dreadful mountains, iron clubs, and trees, churning up the waters, they rose to a height of a hundred yojanas.
